exercise.name: Decline Leg Raise
steps: Lie on a decline bench with your head at the high end.
Hold the bench behind your head and keep your legs straight.
Raise your legs until they point up, then lower them slowly.
exercise.one_line_summary: Lying face up on a 20 deg decline bench, head at the high end, hands holding the bench behind the head. Straight legs rise from just above the body line to pointing straight up (hip flexion ~100 deg), then lower. Abs are the target; hip flexors do much of the lift.

setup.target: Decline bench 20 deg; lying head up the slope.
setup.why: Library step 1. S1: the reverse crunch on a 30 deg incline was among the highest RA exercises.

setup.target: Fists hold the bench uprights behind the head, elbows up.
setup.why: Library step 2: anchors the upper body.

movement.measure: angle of the straight legs to the trunk
movement.start: ~10 deg (heels just off the pad end)

muscles.emg: Inclined reverse crunch among the highest for upper and lower RA (S1); leg raise works the abs (S2).
muscles.role: Holds the pelvis and curls it up at the top.
muscles.surface: The two vertical bands down the front of the belly, lower ribs to the pubic bone.

muscles.emg: High in the inclined reverse crunch (S1); the leg raise raised hip-flexor EMG (S2).
muscles.role: Lifts the legs; listed, not lit (the app lists abs only).
muscles.surface: Front of the hip and the top of the thigh.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Knees fold as the legs rise.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Library step 2 says legs straight; the lever gets shorter.

sources.citation: Escamilla RF, Babb E, DeWitt R, et al. 2006. Electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training. Phys Ther 86(5):656-671. doi:10.1093/ptj/86.5.656
sources.what_it_gave: Hanging knee-up with straps and the reverse crunch inclined 30 deg are among the highest for upper/lower rectus abdominis, obliques and latissimus; rectus femoris high in the inclined reverse crunch and bent-knee sit-up.

sources.citation: Kim K, Lee T. 2016. Comparison of muscular activities in the abdomen and lower limbs while performing sit-up and leg-raise. J Phys Ther Sci 28(2):491-494. doi:10.1589/jpts.28.491
sources.what_it_gave: Sit-up vs leg raise (upper/lower RA, external oblique, rectus femoris, iliopsoas): the eccentric sit-up raised abdominal activity most; the leg raise and eccentric sit-up raised hip-flexor activity.
The steps the app shows; the pictures must match them.

clip_check.check: Head and pelvis on the pad in both
End legs vertical, start legs near the body line
